Subject: Pinebridge: selecting ingress path for private deployment (peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN)

Alex — thanks for the call this morning. Per Pinebridge's security and residency constraints, you asked us to propose a primary network ingress approach for Redwood Private in your us-east-1 account and a fallback path. High level requirements you reiterated:

- Dedicated private connectivity (no public endpoints in the critical path)
- Support for sustained 1 Gbps bursty traffic from inference clients + predictable tail latency
- Auditability: flow logs, connection details preserved for SOC/ISO audit
- Minimal cross-account routing headaches for your infra team

Attached is an initial diagram and an outline of the tradeoffs — asking internal folks to chime in below.

Asks for Pinebridge: can you confirm the BGP contact for your on-prem edge (if we do S2S) and the target steady-state throughput we should size for? Also confirm whether you require cross-account peering (Redwood hosted VPC peered into your account) or prefer a consumer model (we host endpoint in our account and you connect to it).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Technical PoC: spin up PrivateLink endpoint in a PoC VPC + run latency/throughput tests (2 weeks)
2) Fallback plan: configure S2S VPN between your edge and Redwood Private if PrivateLink cannot satisfy requirements or policy
3) Commercial: Marissa to draft MAA (mutual action plan) with throughput bands and pricing

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Pinebridge: selecting ingress path for private deployment (peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN)

Thanks Ethan — quick engineering summary of the options and my initial recommendation. I'll keep it focused on operational constraints and observable limits.

VPC Peering (cross-account peering):
- Pros: Direct L3 connectivity, low additional cost, no proxies in data path.
- Cons: Not transitive (would need peering per VPC), you can run into 50+ peering connections if customers scale; security model is broader (CIDR exposure) and harder to lock down for per-tenant access.
- Perf: Good for high-throughput, low-latency intra-VPC traffic; however, cross-account route table management and propagation can be operationally heavy for Pinebridge's networking team.

PrivateLink (AWS NLB + Interface endpoints):
- Pros: Endpoint as a service — strong isolation, per-service endpoint, works well across accounts without broad route exposure. Supports AWS PrivateLink + SG-level controls. Easier for audit since each endpoint is explicit.
- Cons: Per-ENI costs + hourly/GB charges on AWS; some additional latency due to extra hop through the endpoint. Maximum bandwidth per ENI can be limiting, but you can scale by adding multiple endpoints/NLBs.
- Perf: Slightly higher p99 latencies vs peering in our tests (see attached spreadsheet), but consistent and easier to secure.

Site-to-Site VPN (IPSec / BGP):
- Pros: Works well for on-prem connectivity and regulated environments where a formal BGP session is required. Doesn't require cross-account VPC configuration on the customer's side if they prefer a single VPN tunnel to our gateway.
- Cons: Typically higher variable latency and jitter; throughput depends on customer appliance; requires BGP ops and monitoring. Not ideal as the only ingress for high throughput inference unless you have an MPLS/DirectConnect layer.

Recommendation: PrivateLink as the primary ingress for Pinebridge, with S2S VPN as a documented fallback. PrivateLink gives us the clean audit and per-endpoint security Pinebridge needs. For the throughput target you mentioned (1 Gbps sustained with occasional spikes), we'll architect multiple NLBs/endpoints across AZs and validate in PoC.

PoC checklist (technical):
- Create PrivateLink service backed by dedicated NLBs in our Private account
- Provision interface endpoints in Pinebridge's VPC (their networking to create)
- Run synthetic workload with TLS + real-request shapes; capture p50/p95/p99
- Collect VPC flow logs + VPC Traffic Mirroring if Pinebridge wants packet-level capture

I'll start drafting a runbook and coordinate with infra for ENI scaling.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Alex — good summary from Ethan and Karthik. A few commercial points to make the PoC and subsequent commitment smooth: 

1) Pricing impact: PrivateLink has additional AWS costs (interface endpoint hourly/GB + NLB) which we typically pass through in the Dedicated/Private SKU. We'll include estimated bands in the MAA.
2) SLA: If Pinebridge needs a hard network latency SLA (e.g., p99 < 120ms), we should capture that in the RTO/RPO section and scope Dedicated capacity nodes to meet it.
3) Onboarding timeline: once Pinebridge confirms BGP contact and approves PoC, we can schedule the PoC in 10 business days.

I'll attach a draft MAA (see MAA-draft-20270409.pdf) and propose these next steps:
- Confirm PoC start date (target week of Apr 26)
- Agree on throughput bands and measurable acceptance criteria (latency/retention/audit logs)
- Assign primary contact for certificates and endpoint provisioning at Pinebridge

Thanks — I'll follow up with a HubSpot update.

Thanks all — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from Pinebridge's side: 

- Our security team prefers the model where we have explicit interface endpoints (PrivateLink) rather than broad peering. They want per-service controls and clear billing attribution.
- For VPN fallback: our edge uses two Juniper SRX appliances with BGP; contact is netops@pinebridge.ai and they can provide ASN and BGP neighbors.
- Egress: we need to ensure that any outbound calls from Redwood nodes to third-party APIs are documented and routable via our egress filters. Is there a recommended pattern to guarantee egress IP stability?

Timeline: we can commit to the week of Apr 26 for PoC. Please include your preferred install runbook and a short checklist for our network team. Also loop in Docs/Legal early for MAA signature.

—Alex Turner
Head of Platform | Pinebridge Analytics

Subject: Re: Pinebridge: selecting ingress path for private deployment (peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN)

Alex — thanks for the clarity. Summary and agreed plan below.

Decision: propose PrivateLink as primary ingress (per-service interface endpoints) + S2S VPN (BGP) as documented fallback. Rationale: meets Pinebridge audit and security needs, avoids broad CIDR exposure, and gives us deterministic per-endpoint controls. We'll size multiple NLBs/ENIs for the 1 Gbps steady-state target and validate in PoC.

Egress IP stability: we will provide a small set of egress NAT IPs per AZ that you can allowlist. For high-assurance egress (customer-dedicated IPs), we can route via a dedicated NAT fleet or peered Transit Gateway; I'll include options in the runbook.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Karthik: prepare PoC runbook + ENI scaling plan (due Apr 15)
- Pinebridge netops (netops@pinebridge.ai): provide ASN, BGP neighbors, and preferred endpoint subnets by Apr 16
- Marissa: finalize MAA and commercial bands (target Apr 19)
- Olga: gather SOC2 flow log exports and our standard audit artifacts for Pinebridge review

Links: DocuSign MAA placeholder: https://docusign.com/MAA/PB-2027-091 (placeholder)

I'll open a ticket (INF-412) and create a shared folder with runbook and test results. Thanks everyone — I'll kick off Karthik's PoC tasks once we receive the netops details.
